headline: Highest risk is capability conflict: both agents can touch files, but prompt-injection and leakage are limited by the audio agent’s no-files/no-network defaults.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: A can read/write files and its sandboxing says skills “reference each other and build on shared context,” so malicious content in shared files could influence A. B has no filesystem, clipboard, MCP, or stdin/stdout surfaces, so it is not a practical injection bridge. The pair risk is therefore limited and not default-crossing.
conditions: IF agent_b gains a file or clipboard bridge to agent_a, injection risk increases.
IF agent_a consumes untrusted shared files as instructions, attacker content can steer its outputs.
mitigations: Keep agent_a’s shared skill files read-only during runs.
Store untrusted inputs outside agent_a’s workspace.
Review any file content before agent_a processes it.
Do not add clipboard or MCP bridges between the agents.

B_data_leakage.rationale: A touches marketing content and product marketing context and can egress to allowlisted APIs, but B has no network egress and no file read surface. There is no documented shared workspace or authenticated principal, so direct leakage from A to B is not evidenced. The main risk is limited to A handling sensitive marketing material locally.
conditions: IF agent_a is given confidential marketing assets, those assets may be exposed to its allowlisted APIs.
IF a shared workspace is introduced, leakage risk rises.
mitigations: Exclude secrets and customer data from agent_a inputs.
Restrict agent_a allowlist to necessary domains only.
Keep agent_b offline and fileless as configured.
Separate workspaces for each agent.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: A can write the filesystem and spawn subprocesses, while B cannot write files, modify git, or spawn subprocesses. That makes direct write-write conflict unlikely, but A’s multiple-instance support and shared file surfaces can still create collisions if both are pointed at the same directory by the operator. Uncertainty is limited but not zero, so medium fits.
conditions: IF both agents are configured to write the same directory, file collisions can occur.
IF agent_a instances run concurrently on shared state, overwrites become possible.
mitigations: Assign separate output directories.
Disable concurrent runs of agent_a on shared artifacts.
Keep git state outside agent_a’s writable paths.
Use per-run temp folders.

D_cascading_error.rationale: A produces marketing content, and B is an audio-speech model with no action-taking or file-write authority. There is no evidence that B treats A’s output as authoritative or that A’s output is automatically fed into B. Without a documented handoff, the cascade pathway is weak and the blast radius is small.
conditions: IF an orchestrator feeds A’s text directly into B as a transcript, B may propagate A’s errors.
IF B is used to generate downstream artifacts from A’s output, verification gaps matter.
mitigations: Insert a human review step between agents.
Do not auto-chain A’s outputs into B.
Require source citations for any claims A generates.
Keep B in transcription-only mode.

E_compliance.rationale: A handles marketing and product marketing context, while B handles audio and speech; no PHI, EU PII, or residency-sensitive data class is documented for either. Because the pair is open-source and unverified, compliance risk is mostly about mismatched retention or logging if operators route sensitive content through A’s allowlisted APIs. B’s lack of network and file access reduces the compliance surface.
conditions: IF regulated data is routed through agent_a’s allowlisted APIs, residency or retention obligations may apply.
IF operators store transcripts or marketing assets in shared logs, retention mismatch can occur.
mitigations: Avoid regulated data in both agents.
Disable or minimize logging for runs.
Document retention for any stored outputs.
Keep agent_b offline for sensitive workloads.
